reasoning_content:
Let's set up Keycloak using the admin REST API:
1. Create the realm "my-realm"
2. Create the client "strassennamen", and set the following:
   - Root URL / Home URL: http://localhost:4200
   - Valid redirect URIs: http://localhost:4200/*, http://localhost:5000/*
   - Valid post logout redirect URIs: http://localhost:4200/*
   - Web Origins: http://localhost:4200 (and +)
   - Standard flow: true, direct access grants: true, implicit flow: true
   - Service accounts (client authentication): false, authorization: false
3. Create client roles app-access, editor
4. Create a test user, map the roles, and set a password

Let's write a script for this.

action.command: cd /tmp && curl -s -c kc-cookies.txt -X POST "http://localhost:8080/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token" -d "client_id=admin-cli" -d "grant_type=password" -d "username=admin" -d "password=admin" -o kc-token.json && jq -r .access_token kc-token.json > kc-token.txt && echo "TOKEN OK" && TOKEN=$(cat kc-token.txt) && curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/realms -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"realm":"my-realm","enabled":true}' -w "\nHTTP:%{http_code}\n"

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /tmp && curl -s -c kc-cookies.txt -X POST \"http://localhost:8080/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token\" -d \"client_id=admin-cli\" -d \"grant_type=password\" -d \"username=admin\" -d \"password=admin\" -o kc-token.json && jq -r .access_token kc-token.json > kc-token.txt && echo \"TOKEN OK\" && TOKEN=$(cat kc-token.txt) && curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/realms -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"realm\":\"my-realm\",\"enabled\":true}' -w \"\\nHTTP:%{http_code}\\n\"", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Create my-realm realm in Keycloak"}
